{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABcqkg6g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhGMtIc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 219, "title": "Add Live Button input nodes and optional event-triggered Hold emission for manual graph actions", "body": "## Goal

Allow a user to press a configurable button in the Chrome extension **Live → Graph Actions** area to trigger any graph path, without coupling Button to text or to summarization. The motivating example is **manual, on-demand TextSummary**: transcription continues to accumulate and display normally, but the summary does not run on every transcript update.

**Implement only through the existing Node/Port event delivery mechanism** (ordinary `context.emit(...)`), not a special “run summary” API or a new side-channel event engine.

## Intended graph

```text
ASR.final ──→ TextAccumulator.append
                       │
             TextAccumulator.text
                  ├─────────────────────→ Display.input1  (transcript tab)
                  │
                  └─────────────────────→ Hold.input
                                         Hold.value ───→ TextSummary.text
Button.trigger ─────────────────────────→ Hold.trigger      │
                                                            └─→ Display.input2 (summary tab)
```

The existing Display tab contract is **one input = one selectable tab** (#216); this issue must not reintroduce side-by-side input columns.

## 1. Button: generic source node

- Node type `Button`, Graph Editor category **Sources / inputs**, **no input ports**.
- One ordinary output port, e.g. `trigger: NUMBER`, emitting a lightweight marker such as `1` on **every** click. **No new dedicated TRIGGER contract is required.** Repeated identical values are distinct deliveries, not deduplicated.
- Text setting `label` defines the Live button caption (e.g. “Generate summary”); sensible nonempty fallback if blank, appropriate validation/length and Save/Load/Import/Export persistence.
- Live automatically renders buttons associated with executable Button nodes, ordered deterministically and addressed by stable **node ID**, not label. Duplicate captions cannot mix actions.
- Initial placement: a simple **Graph Actions** area in Live near the existing Start/Stop/Cancel recording controls. **No per-button absolute coordinates, free-form layout editor, extra placement settings, or Graph Editor-coordinate-to-Live mapping.** Layout may be extended separately later.
- Clicks in a running session emit through the correct live Pipeline node context. No emissions into a stale, canceled or replaced session. Disable or visibly explain unavailable buttons during loading/not running, cancellation and failure; prevent repeated UI clicks accidentally becoming unowned async work. Do not tie the button to audio capture permissions.
- The existing `INPUT_TYPES` collection is currently for audio inputs and powers capture permission/source logic; integrate Button as a source for graph execution **without accidentally treating it as an audio source**.

## 2. Extend existing Hold, not a new TriggerGate/Sample node

Port contract:

| Port | Direction | Contract | Semantics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | input | `TEXT` | Store latest value; **never emits** by itself |
| `trigger` | input, **optional** | input-only wildcard `ANY` (or equivalent) | React to **arrival of any connected output delivery** regardless of payload |
| `value` | **the only output** | `TEXT` | Preserve sampled behavior when trigger is disconnected; emit latest held TEXT on trigger when connected |

**Mode A — Hold.trigger not connected (backward compatibility):**
- Keep **exactly the old Hold semantics**: `input` stores latest TEXT; `value` is a sampled output read alongside another ordinary input to a consumer; no unsolicited emit.
- Existing Hold/TextFormatter/TextSummary feedback graphs remain valid and behave exactly as before.

**Mode B — Hold.trigger connected:**
- `input` updates the latest stored TEXT **silently**, including during repeated transcript updates.
- Each event arriving on `trigger` causes exactly one **ordinary emission** on the same `value` output containing a snapshot of the latest stored TEXT. Ignore the trigger's payload.
- **Do not add a second output port**. In this mode `value` behaves as a normal emitted output, **not simultaneously as a sampled output**. No double-delivery.
- The mere existence of the trigger connection enables this behavior; its payload contents (empty string, zero, identical repeated value, etc.) must not suppress firing.
- A trigger before the first input must not accidentally start an empty TextSummary job. Define a deterministic “no value yet” behavior (recommended: no emit and a visible/accessible inactive state), while preserving empty-string input as a valid explicitly received TEXT value if needed by a generic downstream consumer.
- Processing order matters. Take the held value **at the trigger's actual admitted/processed event boundary**, not later when async generation completes. If `input` and `trigger` arrive in one atomic grouped delivery, apply the new `input` first and emit once. Preserve deterministic FIFO for otherwise independent producers; no surprising replays or delayed emissions.
- Multiple trigger deliveries each represent their own event. Respect existing Pipeline queue/admission and async provenance/lifecycle; don't invent deduplication or silently drop events. For downstream expensive jobs, apply bounded/visible busy handling at the appropriate level rather than causing unbounded queued summaries.

## 3. Generic wildcard input contract

- A trigger should accept **ordinary TEXT or NUMBER emissions as well as Button outputs**. Ideally it can accept any existing concrete output type; being connected to `trigger` means *delivery occurred*, not *interpret this value*.
- Current `ITEM` is a restricted display-oriented union, **not ANY**; do not misuse/expand `ITEM` to make trigger connections work.
- Introduce an **input-only, sink-side wildcard contract** (`ANY` or equivalent) with explicit validation rules, preserving existing strict contracts for all other ports and not allowing wildcard outputs to bypass type checks.
- Ensure that trigger-side delivery avoids expensive unnecessary copying or interpreting large audio/structured payloads where possible, while preserving safe queue/event accounting. Every arriving emission is a distinct trigger, even if its payload equals a previous value.

## 4. Pipeline, graph analysis and lifecycle integration

- The current Pipeline treats `sampledOutputs` as a fixed property and builds sampled routes, topology and feedback reachability during construction. **Determine whether `Hold.value` is sampled or ordinary per Hold instance from the saved graph's connected `trigger` port**, consistently in graph validation/executable-path selection, Pipeline construction, scheduling and node creation. Do not just call `emit('value', ...)` on a still-sampled output.
- Preserve valid pre-existing feedback graphs in mode A. In mode B, normal event-cycle detection must apply; never allow a realtime feedback loop merely because the same Hold was previously sampled.
- Avoid treating input-only updates as regular output events; no rerunning TextSummary on changes to accumulator text.
- Ensure the graph execution selector retains a connected Button source and manually gated path; it must not prune the button or gate as unreachable when audio is the other root.
- The UI can fire only after the relevant Pipeline is started. Use the session's live context/cancel signal; preserve Stop draining, Cancel rejecting/discarding pending events, restart/reset and stale button safety.
- Multiple Button nodes and multiple Hold instances must remain independent; one Button's output can fan out through ordinary graph edges.

## 5. Goal-specific behavior: manual summarization

- ASR → TextAccumulator and the normal display path continue updating while TextSummary receives **no** new input until a trigger.
- When the user presses **Generate summary**, the summary receives exactly one snapshot of the currently accumulated text and produces a result in the other Display tab.
- A second button press should be a distinct request, with explicit bounded/busy behavior appropriate to TextSummary (no accidental simultaneous inference or unlimited queue).
- Current TextSummary model startup loads resources at **session Start**, even if no manual request happens. This can still contend with transcription. Investigate deferring model/Worker initialization until first triggered work (or another safe explicit initialization strategy); document the chosen behavior and any remaining startup cost. The fundamental requirement is that **inference itself never runs until a user-triggered delivery**.
- Current TextSummary has an input cap of **32,768 UTF-16 characters** and rejects longer text without truncating. Preserve honest errors and do not silently summarize an arbitrary prefix. The long-recording problem can be an explicitly separated follow-up if needed; do not invent hidden truncation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Graph Editor exposes `Button` under Sources / inputs with a configurable caption and an ordinary output port; Live Graph Actions renders exactly the buttons represented by active graph nodes.
- [ ] Clicking a Live button fires exactly one typed `emit` on its node's output; no special processing API or inference coupling.
- [ ] `Hold.trigger` accepts at least `TEXT` and `NUMBER` output connections without relaxing other typed ports, and repeated identical emits still trigger.
- [ ] `Hold.input` updates never emit. With trigger connected, `Hold.value` emits the latest stored snapshot exactly once per trigger, **with only one output port**.
- [ ] With trigger disconnected, unchanged Hold sampled/feedback functionality and graph validation pass unchanged.
- [ ] Explicit tests for typed graph validation, sampled-vs-emitted routing, cycle detection, grouped/independent delivery order, missing initial value, fan-out, multiple buttons, busy/duplicate clicks, error/Stop/Cancel/restart and stale-session interactions.
- [ ] In the manual-summary fixture, ASR/transcription and accumulation continue without auto-running the summary; only the button triggers it, and the result appears in the correct Display input tab.
- [ ] Keyboard and touch accessibility and 390px/narrow-window Graph Actions layout work; no dependence on node coordinates.
- [ ] Add unit and packaged Chrome-extension integration tests, documentation and a concrete example graph; report what was actually run and any browser/performance limitations.

## Likely touch points

- `web/port-contracts.js` (input-only wildcard and compatibility)
- `web/hold-node.js` (optional trigger mode, unchanged single `value` output)
- `web/pipeline.js` (sampled routing vs ordinary event emission, lifecycle and sequencing)
- `extension/graph.js` (Button/Hold definitions, dynamic sampled-mode graph analysis, source classification)
- `extension/graph-runtime.js`, `extension/session.js` (Button context and dispatch, session ownership)
- `extension/graph-editor.js` (Button Source category, Settings/help)
- `extension/recorder.html`, `extension/recorder.js`, `extension/recorder.css` (Graph Actions)
- `tests/*`, docs/examples and graph architecture docs

**Scope:** deliver generic Button-driven events and extend Hold's existing sole output for optional trigger-based emission. Do not add `ManualTextTrigger`, `Sample`, `TriggerGate`, a second Hold output, or a new UI layout engine.
